Issues - U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers Issues Home Issues Appropriations Rogers served as Chairman of the House Appropriations Committee from 2011 to 2016, where he pioneered the path for historic discretionary spending cuts, rigorous oversight, and an open, transparent process.  Keep Reading  >> Economic Development In his 32 years in Congress, Rogers has been committed to supporting projects that promote economic development, job creation, a stronger infrastructure, and a better standard of living for Kentuckians in the 5th Congressional District and nationwide. Rogers was instrumental in standing up the Southeast Kentucky Economic Development Corporation which offers local businesses low interest loans, business development assistance, and technical advice.  Keep Reading  >> Education One of Rogers’ top priorities is to provide our best and brightest students from southern and eastern Kentucky top-notch educational and career training opportunities to stay at home, start and grow local businesses, participate in civic, cultural and faith-based organizations, and realize their future belongs in the region.  Keep Reading  >> Energy Rogers has been a strong advocate in Congress for advancing our nation's domestic energy production, particularly safe and environmentally-responsible coal mining. For over 30 years, Rogers has dedicated himself to advancing Kentucky energy jobs, keeping energy and gas prices low, and strengthening our nation’s energy security. Congressman Rogers Votes to Protect Mining in America - Press Releases - U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Congressman Rogers Votes to Protect Mining in America Sep 02 2026 WASHINGTON, DC –  U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) voted for the Protecting Domestic Mining Act ( H.R. 1501 ) on Wednesday to expedite permitting for American mining and mineral processing.  “We need to strengthen mining in America, not only to create jobs in the coal industry and lower energy rates, but to empower the U.S. supply chain from mining to manufacturing. Products that are Made in America, ultimately start with Mining in America,”  said Congressman Rogers, Dean of the House . “This bill streamlines the permitting process and clears roadblocks for American production, so we don’t have to rely on foreign countries for raw materials.”  Last year, the  United States depended  on imports for more than half of its supply of 54 non-fuel mineral commodities, giving other countries leverage over American workers, manufacturers and national security.  H.R. 1501 permanently makes domestic mining and mineral processing eligible sectors for FAST-41. It does not waive environmental laws, eliminate required reviews, or guarantee a permit.  The bill passed the House and now moves on to the Senate for consideration.  For more information about Congressman Rogers’ work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on social media.

Congress Passes Federal Funding Extension to Avoid Government Shutdown - Press Releases - U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Congress Passes Federal Funding Extension to Avoid Government Shutdown Sep 01 2026 WASHINGTON, DC --  U.S. Rep. Harold "Hal" Rogers (KY-05) voted for the Senate Amendment to the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2026, H.R. 6500, to extend current federal funding through December 11, 2026. The bipartisan stopgap funding bill avoids a government shutdown ahead of the end of the fiscal year on September 30, 2026.  "We voted to keep the government open and running for the American people, removing any fear of losing federal pay, benefits or services from a government shutdown,"  said Congressman Rogers, Chairman Emeritus of the House Appropriations Committee . "Our work on the House Appropriations Committee has been thorough and efficient, reporting all 12 federal funding bills for fiscal year 2027 out of committee for consideration by the House, where three have already been approved. This extension provides additional time for the House and Senate to finalize all 12 federal funding bills with thoughtful investments of taxpayer dollars."  The clean, bipartisan bill passed by a vote of 370 to 48 and now moves on to President Trump's desk for signature.  For more information about Congressman Rogers' work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit  halrogers.house.gov  and follow him on  social media .

Congressman Rogers Breaks Ground at High School Alma Mater for New Development in Wayne County - Press Releases - U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers U.S. Congressman Hal Rogers Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Congressman Rogers Breaks Ground at High School Alma Mater for New Development in Wayne County Aug 26 2026 Monticello, KY –  U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) joined state and local officials for a ground-breaking ceremony at his high school alma mater, the former Wayne County High School’s AJ Lloyd Building. The building will be renovated into a new outdoor community center and farmer’s market. Another building on-site will become the new home of Provalus, a technology company that will be able to expand from 140 to 200 jobs in Monticello. The estimated cost to renovate the AJ Lloyd Building is $4.7 million. Congressman Rogers secured $4 million in federal Community Project Funding in 2024.  “This historic building in my home county is a landmark in my memories. It’s the place where teachers, friends and community leaders molded my beliefs, work ethic, and inspired my desire to serve others. This building has served countless families in Wayne County well over the years, and now, it will be a recreational centerpiece for the community, with a technology hub next door,”  said Congressman Rogers, Dean of the House . “The dual purpose of this property paves the way for more jobs in Wayne County, and a beautiful place for local families to enjoy for generations.”  “It’s a great time to be in Monticello! When this historic building is renovated, it will honor the past and make way for future opportunities.
